document.title: Motion to Intervene and Comments of Base Power Inc. re PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.’s 07/31/2026 filing

pages.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
 
 
) 
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
) 
 
 
Docket No. ER26-3380-000 
 
) 
 
MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS  
OF BASE POWER INC. 
Pursuant to Rules 211, 212, and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s 
(Commission) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 Base Power, Inc. (Base) respectfully submits this 
motion to intervene, together with comments on the filing of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) 
establishing the Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP), dated July 31, 2026.2 
Base supports the RBP and the overall structure of the proposed auction.  Following the 
capacity shortfalls from the last few auctions, PJM and its staff should be commended for 
developing the RBP proposal on a compressed timeline to address the region’s needs.  Base 
particularly appreciates PJM’s positive and constructive engagement with stakeholders on the 
peak-shaving opt-out structure.  Establishing the peak-shaving opt-out to reduce the Initial RBP 
Target unlocks a key pathway to address the capacity shortage, mitigate system-wide costs, and 
reduce risks to ratepayers. 
In these comments, Base requests two narrow drafting clarifications related to the peak 
shaving opt-out in proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.1(d).3  PJM’s clarification of these 
 
1 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.211, 385.212, 385.214 (2026). 
2 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address Resource Adequacy Concerns 
Stemming from Large Loads, Docket No. ER26-3380-000 (filed July 31, 2026) (RBP Filing). 
3 Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, § 18.1(d).

2 
 
two items will ensure the peak-shaving opt-out functions as intended, giving effect to state laws 
that contemplate demand-flexibility programs, including contracted peak shaving. 
First, Base requests PJM to clarify that the peak-shaving decrement is not discounted and 
will have a 1:1 ratio; in other words, every 1 MW of peak-shaving identified by an Electric 
Distributor will result in 1 MW decremented from the Initial RBP Target, with no adjustments.  
This clarification by PJM—easily effectuated by the removal of the phrase “up to” in Attachment 
DD Section 18.1(d)—will allow large loads to estimate the value of a commercial contract with 
peak-shaving providers and have confidence in finalizing those commercial arrangements without 
delay. 
Second, Base seeks clarification from PJM that, to qualify for the peak-shaving opt-out in 
the RBP, the deadline for any Peak Shaving Adjustment plan submitted pursuant to the 
requirements of Attachment DD-2 will be the September 2027 deadline (to be effective for the 
2028/2029 Delivery Year), not September 2026. 
I. 
MOTION TO INTERVENE 
Rule 214 permits intervention where the movant “has or represents an interest which may 
be directly affected by the outcome of the proceeding[.]”4 
Base meets that standard.  Base is an energy technology company that deploys distributed 
battery storage and aggregates its resources to provide energy and grid services, along with backup 
power for residential consumers.5  Base’s interest in this proceeding is direct and concrete.  Base 
is pursuing commercial arrangements in the PJM region that depend on the peak-shaving opt-out 
established in section 18.1(d).  The two clarifications identified below determine whether those 
 
4 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(2). 
5 Base Power in the press, available at https://www.basepowercompany.com/press.

3 
 
arrangements can participate in the opt-out. Base’s interests would not be adequately represented 
by any other party.   
This motion is timely filed within the intervention period established by the Commission.  
Base respectfully requests that the Commission grant this motion to intervene with full party status, 
and reserves the right to file comments, protests, answers, and briefs in this proceeding. 
II. 
COMMENTS IN SUPPORT AND REQUESTS FOR CLARIFICATION 
Base supports PJM’s RBP proposal and appreciates PJM’s positive engagement with 
stakeholders on the peak-shaving opt-out structure.  The success of PJM’s RBP proposal, 
particularly the peak-shaving opt-out provision, will depend on whether its implementation can be 
harmonized with qualifying peak-shaving programs established in PJM States, including those 
enacted by statutes in both New Jersey and Virginia.  This coordination reflects the cooperative 
federalism approach that PJM has taken in recent reforms, and Base appreciates PJM’s willingness 
to work with stakeholders on these issues.  
Below, Base describes how state statutes like the newly enacted NJ Data Center Fair Share 
Act (DCFSA)6 and Va. Code Ann. § 56-596.7 (2026) create avenues for Electric Distributors and 
large loads to reduce demand during peak periods by delivering, funding, or procuring peak-
shaving measures from other customers.  These state programs are consistent with the RBP peak-
shaving opt-out and can be given full effect by PJM, so long as that opt-out is appropriately 
structured.  With the two narrow clarifications requested herein, the PJM RBP proposal and the 
state laws will work together to their fullest, complementary potential, to the benefit of all 
stakeholders.  Base does not object to other aspects of the RBP filing. 
 
6 The DCFSA (S731/A796) was signed into law on July 7, 2026 and has not yet been printed into a chapter law.  
N.J. P.L.2026, C.32 (July 7, 2026) (to be codified at N.J. Rev. Stat. Title 48).  The Fourth Reprint is available at 
https://pub.njleg.state.nj.us/Bills/2026/A1000/796_R4.PDF.

4 
 
A. 
PJM’s Peak-Shaving Opt-Out Recognizes and Gives Effect to Efforts By 
States To Establish Peak-Shaving Adjustment Programs. 
Policymakers and regulators across the country are working diligently within their 
respective jurisdictions to address unprecedented energy demand, striving to preserve the 
reliability and affordability of energy for everyday Americans. Coordinating these overlapping 
efforts will amplify their effectiveness, to the benefit of ratepayers.  PJM’s peak-shaving opt-out 
does precisely this by appropriately recognizing state-authorized peak-shaving programs, in a 
manner consistent with ordinary-course capacity-procurement auctions in PJM. Two such state-
authorized peak-shaving programs are emblematic of this opportunity. 
In Virginia, Va. Code Ann. § 56-596.7 establishes a framework for “voluntary demand 
flexibility program[s]” under which large loads may partner with third parties to peak-shave in 
order to maximize or reasonably maximize “electric grid system savings and improve reliability 
for retail electric service customers.”7 The law expressly states that under such programs, large 
loads may “secure measurable and verifiable electric load reductions from other retail electric 
service customers during time periods of peak system demand or other events that cause strain on 
the electric grid,”8 directly authorizing large loads to contract with, fund, or purchase peak-shaving 
measures from third parties under the program.  
Similarly, New Jersey codified its peak-shaving programs in the DCFSA, which Governor 
Sherrill signed into law on July 7, 2026.9  The DCFSA establishes a demand-reduction program 
for “data center customers [to] contract directly with a third party for, or otherwise fund, verified 
 
7 Va. Code Ann. § 56-596.7(B)(1) (utilities); § 56-596.7(C)(1) (cooperatives).  
8 Id. § 56-596.7(A) (defining “[d]emand flexibility”). 
9 Press Release, Office of the Governor, Governor Sherrill Announces Ratepayer Relief, Signs Major Legislation on 
Energy, Saving New Jerseyans $1B Annually (July 7, 2026), 
https://www.nj.gov/governor/news/2026/20260707a.shtml.

5 
 
demand flexibility by other customers on the same electric public utility system.”10  The 
Governor’s Office described the mechanism as a program “through which a new large load offsets 
its capacity obligation by paying to reduce demand elsewhere on the system,” and characterized it 
as “the first of its kind, driving accelerated deployment of distributed energy resources paid for by 
data centers.”11  
The DCFSA was drafted to operate in conjunction with PJM’s capacity market 
mechanisms, including the RBP.  The statute provides that the demand-reduction trade program 
must be designed “for compatibility with the load forecasting methods of the regional transmission 
organization, the Peak Shaving Adjustment of the regional transmission organization, or any 
similar mechanism used to reduce capacity needs, so that demand reductions verified under the 
program are reflected in the load forecast used by the regional transmission organization to procure 
capacity, including any capacity procured under a backstop auction or similar mechanism.”12  In 
other words, the DCFSA explicitly contemplates coordination with PJM capacity-market 
mechanisms, including a backstop auction, directing the NJ BPU and public utilities to promptly 
accept bilateral and multilateral contracts for peak-shaving services so that such peak-shaving can 
be appropriately recognized and accounted for by the deadlines established by PJM’s RBP 
process.13     
 
10 DCFSA § 1.d(4). 
11 Press Release, supra note 9. 
12 DCFSA § 1.d(4)(c). 
13 The DCFSA statute requires each electric public utility to “submit Large Load Adjustments, Peak Shaving 
Adjustments, and customer peak load contribution to the regional transmission organization,” directing its utilities to 
be submitting entities in a manner consistent with the role that proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.1(d) 
assigns to the Electric Distributor.  Id. § 1.b(8); see also id. § 1.h (contracts will be filed with the NJ BPU and “[t]he

6 
 
B. 
Base Requests PJM Make Two Narrow Clarifications on the RBP Proposal. 
To ensure PJM’s peak-shaving opt-out captures these benefits, Base requests that PJM 
make two discrete clarifications to its proposal. 
1. 
Clarification that the Peak-Shaving Decrement is Not Discounted 
First, Base asks PJM to clarify that the peak-shaving amount submitted by the Electric 
Distributor is not discounted.  Section 18.1(d) provides that the Initial RBP Target “shall be further 
decremented . . . by up to the associated MW quantity of load that participates in a peak shaving 
adjustment program.”14 By contrast, the transmittal letter says that “the Initial RBP Target will be 
decremented by the amount specified by the Electric Distributor,”15 which implies a 1:1 decrement 
with no discount.  Likewise, the Tariff’s own structure supports a reading that no discount was 
intended.  The preceding sentence of section 18.1(d) requires that an Electric Distributor’s opt-out 
request “shall specify the associated MW quantity of load in the zone/area that will be opted-out” 
(emphasis added). 
Clarification on the value of the opt-out decrement is needed to allow commercial 
arrangements to be finalized.  Otherwise, Base and other providers that seek to facilitate peak-
shaving cannot determine what decrement a given amount of peak-shaving will produce. And 
without that certainty, peak shaving arrangements with large load counterparties cannot be priced 
or executed.  This clarification can be easily effectuated by removing the phrase “up to” in 
proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, Section 18.1(d), as follows: “shall be further decremented . . . 
 
board shall accept the contract unless the board finds its terms are inconsistent” with certain other provisions of the 
law). 
14 Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, § 18.1(d) (emphasis added). 
15 RBP Filing, Transmittal Letter at 46 (emphasis added).

7 
 
by up to the associated MW quantity of load that participates in a peak shaving adjustment 
program.”   
Placing this clarification in the Tariff rather than in the Manuals is also consistent with how 
the Commission has treated the Peak Shaving Adjustment.  When the Commission accepted the 
Peak Shaving Adjustment in 2019, it directed PJM to move the terms and conditions of that 
program out of Manual 19 and into the Tariff, which is how Attachment DD-2 was created.16   
2. 
Clarification that the Deadline to Meet Attachment DD-2’s Requirements  
  
will be September 2027 
 
Second, Base seeks clarification from PJM that, to qualify for the peak-shaving opt-out in 
the RBP, the deadline for any Peak Shaving Adjustment plan submitted pursuant to the 
requirements of Attachment DD-2 will be September 2027 (to be effective for the 2028/2029 
Delivery Year), not September 2026.  This is a narrow clarification necessary to align the RBP 
opt-out with the procedural deadlines already established in Attachment DD-2.   
Section 18.1(d) conditions the peak-shaving opt-out on programs “that are codified in state 
law and that also meet the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD-2.”17  The challenge is that 
Attachment DD-2 was designed for a different purpose on a different schedule,18 and several of 
its requirements cannot be satisfied in time for the opening of the RBP bid window if not clarified.  
 
16 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 167 FERC ¶ 61,114, at P 55 (2019) (directing PJM to incorporate the Peak Shaving 
Adjustment plan requirements of PJM Manual 19, Attachment D into the Tariff); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 
Compliance Filing, Docket No. ER19-511-002 (filed May 30, 2019); Letter Order, Docket No. ER19-511-002 (June 
26, 2019) (accepting Tariff, Attachment DD-2). 
17 Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, § 18.1(d). 
18 Attachment DD-2 was originally crafted to feed a forecast adjustment into PJM’s load forecast for the annual 
auction cycle.  PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 167 FERC ¶ 61,114, at P 9 (2019) (reciting PJM explanation that the 
Peak Shaving Adjustment is primarily an amendment to PJM’s existing load forecasting methodology).

8 
 
The DCFSA, for example, was signed into law on July 7, 2026, so even though the law expressly 
contemplates participation in the RBP, a September 2026 deadline would be challenging to meet.19 
This clarification would require no Tariff change and arguably follows from Attachment 
DD-2 itself, which ties the September deadline to the “next PJM load forecast update.”  The RBP 
runs on the already-published 2026 PJM Load Forecast.20  So a September 2026 plan would feed 
a forecast that has no bearing on the Initial RBP Target; meanwhile, a September 2027 plan is the 
plan that would apply to the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. Confirming the September 2027 deadline 
would preserve Attachment DD-2’s established procedural framework while providing qualifying 
state-authorized peak-shaving programs a workable path to participate in the RBP, as contemplated 
by Section 18.1(d) and state law. 
 
 
 
19 For example, Attachment DD-2 operates on the annual load forecast cycle, but the PJM RBP opt-out operates on 
the already-published 2026 PJM Load Forecast.  Likewise, a peak shaving program seeking a load forecast 
adjustment must file its plan with PJM no later than ten business days before September 30 in order to be reflected 
in the next PJM load forecast, and eligibility is limited to load reduction programs governed by a tariff or order 
approved by the RERRA.  Attachment DD-2, section A. 
20 See Croop Aff. ¶ 46 (initial allocation based on Load Adjustments “as set forth in PJM Table B9b from the 2026 
PJM Load Forecast”).

9 
 
III. 
CONCLUSION 
For the foregoing reasons, Base respectfully requests that the Commission grant its motion 
to intervene with full party status.  If PJM makes the requested clarifications above, Base requests 
that the Commission approve PJM’s RBP proposal in its entirety. 
Dated: August 21, 2026 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Zina Bash 
Chief Legal Officer
